fields.title: Colon cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Colon cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the large bowel is one of the most common cancers worldwide. Israeli clinics offer a comprehensive approach to treating this disease, using the latest advances in medical science and technology to provide the most effective and gentlest treatment possible.

Diagnosis of colon cancer

  1. Colonoscopy
    the main diagnostic method, allowing the inner surface of the large bowel to be examined and a biopsy taken from any suspicious areas.
  2. Biopsy
    During the colonoscopy a tissue sample is taken, which allows the presence of cancer cells and the type of cancer to be established precisely under the microscope. This is the key method for definitive confirmation of a diagnosis of colon cancer.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Laboratory tests
    a full blood count and tests for tumour markers such as carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and Ca19.9 help assess the presence and activity of cancer cells.
  4. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    are used where necessary to establish the stage of the disease and identify metastases.
  5. PET-CT
    an integrated investigation combining positron emission tomography and computed tomography, for a more precise assessment of the extent of the tumour.

Treatments for colon cancer

  1. Surgery
    removal of the affected part of the bowel is the standard treatment in the early stages of the cancer.
  2. Chemotherapy
    is used to destroy any remaining cancer cells, particularly in advanced cancer or after an operation to reduce the risk of recurrence.
  3. Radiotherapy
    may be used to shrink the tumour before an operation or to destroy any remaining cancer cells afterwards.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    are directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells and at the immune system respectively, offering new possibilities in treating this disease.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of colon cancer

  • An individual approach to every patient makes it possible to design the best treatment programme, taking account of the features of the illness and general health.
  • Advanced medical technology and highly qualified specialists deliver accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • Value for money makes treatment in Israel accessible to many patients, offering high-quality medical care at a competitive price.
  • Particular attention to patients' quality of life after treatment, including recovery and rehabilitation.

Israeli clinics offer the most effective and safe treatments available.

fields.title: Small bowel cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Small bowel cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the small bowel involves the formation of malignant tumours in the small intestine. In Israel, patients are offered advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment aimed at fighting the disease effectively and considerably improving quality of life.

Diagnosis of small bowel cancer

  1. Medical examination and history
    are the first stage, in which doctors assess the patient's symptoms and the history of the illness.
  2. Endoscopy
    including capsule endoscopy and enteroscopy, allows the inner surface of the small bowel to be seen and tumours identified.
  3. Colonoscopy
    is used for a detailed examination of the large bowel, with a biopsy taken afterwards.
  4. Biopsy
    makes it possible to obtain tissue samples for histological analysis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  5. Laboratory tests: blood tests may reveal raised levels of certain tumour markers — carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and CA 19-9 — which may indicate the presence of small bowel cancer. These results help assess the activity of the disease and monitor the response to treatment.
  6. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    are used to assess the stage of the disease and search for metastases.
  7. PET-CT
    may be ordered for a more precise assessment of how far the cancer has spread and for planning treatment.

Treatments for small bowel cancer

  1. Surgery
    the primary and most common treatment. Removal of the tumour together with part of the bowel. It may involve resection of the affected section of bowel.
  2. Chemotherapy
    is used to destroy cancer cells, particularly in advanced cancer or to prevent recurrence.
  3. Radiotherapy
    is used less often than in other types of cancer, but can be effective in shrinking tumours or destroying any cancer cells remaining after surgery.
  4. Targeted therapy
    is directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells, which helps block the growth and spread of the tumour.
  5. Immunotherapy
    uses the mechanisms of the body's immune system to fight the cancer, stimulating or restoring the body's natural ability to fight cancer cells.

Why patients choose Israel for the treatment of small bowel cancer

  • Advanced medical technology and highly qualified specialists in Israel deliver accurate diagnosis and effective treatment.
  • An individual approach to every patient makes it possible to design treatment that best matches the needs and features of each case.
  • Value for money makes Israel an attractive choice for many patients looking for affordable, quality medical care.

Israeli clinics offer a comprehensive approach to the treatment of small bowel cancer, combining the newest medical developments with deep care for the wellbeing of every patient and aiming to extend their lives and improve their quality as far as possible.

fields.title: Urethral cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Urethral cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the urethra is a rare cancer affecting the urinary passage. In Israel, patients are offered innovative methods of diagnosing and treating this type of cancer, which makes it possible to achieve the best results even in difficult cases.

Diagnosis of urethral cancer

  1. Urethroscopy
    Visual examination of the urethra with a special instrument to identify abnormalities or tumours.
  2. Biopsy
    Obtaining a sample of tumour tissue for histological analysis, which is the key to confirming a diagnosis of urethral cancer.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Urine cytology
    Examination of the cells in the urine for cancer cells.
  4. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Help assess how far the tumour has spread within the body.
  5. Ultrasound scan
    Used to assess the state of the bladder, kidneys and surrounding tissues.
  6. Laboratory tests
    Including a full blood count, biochemistry and measurement of tumour markers.
  7. PET-CT
    Combines positron emission tomography and computed tomography for an accurate assessment of how far the cancer has spread. It also establishes the stage of the disease and the effectiveness of treatment.

Treatment of urethral cancer

  1. Surgery
    The main treatment. It may involve partial or complete removal of the urethra, depending on the stage of the disease and the position of the tumour.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Used on its own or in combination with surgery, particularly for tumours that cannot be removed.
  3. Chemotherapy
    May be used to treat metastatic urethral cancer or as an addition to other treatments to reduce the risk of recurrence.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy
    Innovative approaches directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells or at activating the immune system to fight the tumour.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach
    Urologists, oncologists, radiologists and other specialists take part in treatment, ensuring a comprehensive approach to every case.
  • Advanced treatments
    Patients have access to the most modern methods of diagnosis and treatment, including minimally invasive surgical techniques and the latest advances in drug therapy.
  • Highly qualified specialists
    Israeli doctors have international experience and regularly exchange knowledge and practice with colleagues from other countries.
  • An individualised approach to treatment
    Every patient is given a personal treatment programme that takes account of every feature of their condition and their preferences.

Israeli clinics offer patients with urethral cancer access to advanced medical technology and highly qualified care, which makes it possible to achieve the best treatment results and improve patients' quality of life.

fields.title: Vaginal cancer
fields.bodyHtml:
Vaginal cancer: advanced treatment in Israel

Cancer of the vagina is a rare type of cancer that can be diagnosed and treated effectively with modern approaches. Advanced technology and techniques are available in Israel that allow comprehensive treatment of this disease, taking account of the individual circumstances of every patient.

Diagnosis of vaginal cancer:

  1. Gynaecological examination:
    The doctor carries out a visual examination of the vagina and cervix, using special instruments to take a tissue sample for histological analysis.
  2. Biopsy
    Taking a tissue sample for histological examination, which is the gold standard in diagnosis.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  3. Colposcopy:
    Detailed examination of the lining of the vagina and cervix using a special microscope to identify atypical cells.
  4. Transvaginal ultrasound:
    Used to establish the size, shape and structure of the tumour.
  5. MRI and CT:
    Assessment of the extent of the tumour in the pelvis and identification of metastases.
  6. PET-CT:
    The search for active cancer cells in the body and checking for metastases.

Treatments for vaginal cancer:

  1. Surgery:
    • Wide local excision: Removal of the tumour together with some healthy tissue.
    • Vaginectomy: Partial or complete removal of the vagina, depending on the stage and extent of the cancer.
    • Lymphadenectomy: Removal of the regional lymph nodes where metastases are present.
  2. Radiotherapy:
    • Used as the main treatment or in combination with surgery to destroy cancer cells and prevent recurrence.
  3. Chemotherapy:
    • Used to treat advanced cancer or where an operation is not possible. It may be combined with radiotherapy to make it more effective.
  4. Targeted therapy and immunotherapy:
    • The use of the newest medicines directed at specific biological targets in the cancer cells, and activation of the immune system to fight the cancer.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Oncologists, gynaecologists, radiotherapists and surgeons work together to develop the best treatment plan.
  • Advanced medical equipment: The use of the latest advances in medical devices and technology for diagnosis and treatment.
  • Individual treatment: Treatment plans are developed taking account of the stage of the disease, the patient's general health and her personal preferences.

Treatment of vaginal cancer in Israel aims to extend patients' lives and improve their quality as far as possible, delivering high survival rates and minimal side effects.
